comment:
* Represents a contextual mode of the user interface. Action modes can be used to provide * alternative interaction modes and replace parts of the normal UI until finished. * Examples of good action modes include text selection and contextual actions. *
* *

Developer Guides

*

For information about how to provide contextual actions with {@code ActionMode}, * read the Menus * developer guide.

* *

methods.name: public void setTag(Object tag)
methods.comment:
* Set a tag object associated with this ActionMode. * *

Like the tag available to views, this allows applications to associate arbitrary * data with an ActionMode for later reference. * * @param tag Tag to associate with this ActionMode * * @see #getTag()

methods.name: public Object getTag()
methods.comment:
* Retrieve the tag object associated with this ActionMode. * *

Like the tag available to views, this allows applications to associate arbitrary * data with an ActionMode for later reference. * * @return Tag associated with this ActionMode * * @see #setTag(Object)

methods.name: public abstract void setTitle(CharSequence title)
methods.comment:
* Set the title of the action mode. This method will have no visible effect if
     * a custom view has been set.
     *
     * @param title Title string to set
     *
     * @see #setTitle(int)
     * @see #setCustomView(View)

methods.name: public abstract void setTitle(int resId)
methods.comment:
* Set the title of the action mode. This method will have no visible effect if
     * a custom view has been set.
     *
     * @param resId Resource ID of a string to set as the title
     *
     * @see #setTitle(CharSequence)
     * @see #setCustomView(View)

methods.name: public abstract void setSubtitle(CharSequence subtitle)
methods.comment:
* Set the subtitle of the action mode. This method will have no visible effect if
     * a custom view has been set.
     *
     * @param subtitle Subtitle string to set
     *
     * @see #setSubtitle(int)
     * @see #setCustomView(View)

methods.name: public abstract void setSubtitle(int resId)
methods.comment:
* Set the subtitle of the action mode. This method will have no visible effect if
     * a custom view has been set.
     *
     * @param resId Resource ID of a string to set as the subtitle
     *
     * @see #setSubtitle(CharSequence)
     * @see #setCustomView(View)

methods.name: public void setTitleOptionalHint(boolean titleOptional)
methods.comment:
* Set whether or not the title/subtitle display for this action mode * is optional. * *

In many cases the supplied title for an action mode is merely * meant to add context and is not strictly required for the action * mode to be useful. If the title is optional, the system may choose * to hide the title entirely rather than truncate it due to a lack * of available space.

* *

Note that this is merely a hint; the underlying implementation * may choose to ignore this setting under some circumstances.

* * @param titleOptional true if the title only presents optional information.

methods.name: public boolean getTitleOptionalHint()
methods.comment:
* @return true if this action mode has been given a hint to consider the
     *         title/subtitle display to be optional.
     *
     * @see #setTitleOptionalHint(boolean)
     * @see #isTitleOptional()

methods.name: public boolean isTitleOptional()
methods.comment:
* @return true if this action mode considers the title and subtitle fields
     *         as optional. Optional titles may not be displayed to the user.

methods.name: public abstract void setCustomView(View view)
methods.comment:
* Set a custom view for this action mode. The custom view will take the place of
     * the title and subtitle. Useful for things like search boxes.
     *
     * @param view Custom view to use in place of the title/subtitle.
     *
     * @see #setTitle(CharSequence)
     * @see #setSubtitle(CharSequence)

methods.name: public abstract void invalidate()
methods.comment:
* Invalidate the action mode and refresh menu content. The mode's
     * {@link ActionMode.Callback} will have its
     * {@link Callback#onPrepareActionMode(ActionMode, Menu)} method called.
     * If it returns true the menu will be scanned for updated content and any relevant changes
     * will be reflected to the user.

methods.name: public abstract void finish()
methods.comment:
* Finish and close this action mode. The action mode's {@link ActionMode.Callback} will
     * have its {@link Callback#onDestroyActionMode(ActionMode)} method called.

methods.name: public abstract Menu getMenu()
methods.comment:
* Returns the menu of actions that this action mode presents.
     *
     * @return The action mode's menu.

methods.name: public abstract CharSequence getTitle()
methods.comment:
* Returns the current title of this action mode.
     *
     * @return Title text

methods.name: public abstract CharSequence getSubtitle()
methods.comment:
* Returns the current subtitle of this action mode.
     *
     * @return Subtitle text

methods.name: public abstract View getCustomView()
methods.comment:
* Returns the current custom view for this action mode.
     *
     * @return The current custom view

methods.name: public abstract MenuInflater getMenuInflater()
methods.comment: * Returns a {@link MenuInflater} with the ActionMode's context.

methods.name: public boolean isUiFocusable()
methods.comment:
* Returns whether the UI presenting this action mode can take focus or not.
     * This is used by internal components within the framework that would otherwise
     * present an action mode UI that requires focus, such as an EditText as a custom view.
     *
     * @return true if the UI used to show this action mode can take focus
     * @hide Internal use only
